I'd add a 13mm wrench for seat posts, a flat 13mm wrench for adding/removing pedals, some WD40 to easy up rusty parts and to clean greasy parts, and maybe a chain cleaner tool.

Good point about old style saddle clamps, which are often still used on department store bikes. Weirdly, both my old fashioned saddle clamps came with 14mm nuts for some inexplicable reason. I had to go down to the hardware store to get some 13mm nuts just so I would be able to adjust the clamp on the road if needed with a cone wrench I sometimes carry (skinny double sided box wrench, one side 13mm, the other side 15mm). The 15mm side comes in handy for removing or installing pedals and for axles without a quick release.

edit: with regards to degreasing, I find that wd-40 works great, but so does ordinary dish soap in a pinch. Many people also often have something like Awesome Orange or Simple Green lying around, and any cheap off-brand formula should work well enough. I am starting to have doubts about using wd-40 to degrease a chain though. I'm worried that it might actually strip away the factory lube, which may shorten the life of a relatively new chain that would otherwise still have the factory lube intact.

WD40

I have another note about WD40. Some people would use it to clean out parts like gunky shifters and squeaky brake levers, however I find that tri-flow works better for this and can also do a better job of filling many of the same roles as wd40 around the house. Plus it smells good...

Most bike shops, hardware stores, and even locksmiths will carry tri-flow in either a spray or a small drip bottle, so it's not hard to come by, and it can even be used as well-recommended chain lube. But wd-40 still has two main advantages over tri-flow. The first is availability. You can buy wd-40 almost anywhere. The second is portability. You can buy a tiny spray can of wd-40 that's very easy to take with you on a long distance bike trip, and a spray can is best for good penetration.

FYI, wd-40 makes a pretty terrible chain lube for any trip longer than several miles. It's not really meant to be used that way.

WD40 is not suitable to use as lube. Only for cleaning greasy parts and loosening up rusty parts.

For longer term lube, use proper grease or oil. WD40 will disappear quite quickly, leaving moving parts grinding.
